text:
Elaine: quick heads-up — opening a docs PR to harmonize KMS naming across audit export examples and the SOC2 wording. spotted an inconsistency: examples use `kms:key-rot` while SOC2 text references customer-managed keys. can legal + docs take a look?
Raj: yep. paste the raw snippet here so i can check CLI/HTTP fields.
Elaine: snippet from draft (HTTP example):
```
POST /v1/audit/exports
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "destination": "s3://acme-company/audit/2026-03-22",
  "encryption": { "type": "kms", "key": "kms:key-rot" },
  "redaction": ["email", "api_key"]
}
```
Elaine: legal wants the canonical field to indicate customer-managed KMS and we should show the identifier field separately (ARN/id).
Josh (legal): agreed. from compliance POV we must not imply Redwood manages customer keys. please change the example to show `encryption.key_type: "customer-managed-kms"` and add `encryption.kms_key_id: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd..."`. also add a one-liner: customers are responsible for key rotation and access controls.
Raj: makes sense. small SDK note: our python/js samples use a variable named `kms_key` — suggest we standardize on `kms_key_id` in all code examples and keep the user-facing HTTP field names aligned.
Maria: i'll update the SDK snippets and examples folder. i can also add a unit smoke test that imports the example file and ensures it parses (no infra call).
docs-bot: PR draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999 — files touched: docs/security/audit-exports.md, docs/reference/export-api.md, examples/sdk/python/audit_export_example.py
Elaine: thanks. @Josh (legal) can you copy the exact sentence you want for the docs? i'll add it to the PR description so reviewers understand the change.
Josh (legal): suggested sentence (use verbatim): "Customers must supply a customer-managed KMS key (KMS key id or ARN) to encrypt exported audit logs. Redwood does not have access to or rotate customer-managed keys; key lifecycle and rotation policies are the responsibility of the customer."
Raj: i'll run the md lint and example smoke tests. couple of pedants: ensure the fields table in export-api.md lists `encryption.key_type` and `encryption.kms_key_id` and mark the old `encryption.key` as deprecated with migration guidance.
Maria: migration note i plan to add: "Previously: `encryption.key` accepted opaque values. New: prefer `encryption.key_type: "customer-managed-kms"` and `encryption.kms_key_id` for identifier. Update any SDK usage of `kms_key` to `kms_key_id`."
Elaine: i'll push the wording and the updated curl + py examples. pinging docs-bot to add CI once commits are up. :email:
docs-bot: CI checks: docs lint ✅, linkcheck ⚠️ (one old internal legal FAQ link), examples smoke tests ⚠️ (one test marked flaky/xfail).
Elaine: i'll fix the broken link to the legal FAQ and mark the flaky test as xfail in the harness.
Raj: left two tiny comments on the PR re code fence spacing and an inline HTML entity in the md table.
Maria: pushed a commit renaming variables in python example and updating the examples test. PR now has 3 commits.
Josh (legal): approved the in-thread wording; leaving a formal review approval on the PR shortly. ✅
Elaine: thanks all. plan to merge once linkcheck is green and linter is happy. i'll add a docs-site changelog note and a small banner on the audit-export page so customers searching for KMS guidance see the change. :tada:
